sections.title: READ_ME
intro: How the sheets work together: what PROFILE drives, what the evidence grades mean, where training lives, and the live checks the workbook runs on itself.

sections.title: HOW THIS WORKBOOK WORKS
intro: PROFILE is the single input sheet and it drives everything. The dashboard shows what applies to you and hides what does not. PROFILE drives everything The five visibility tags - Sex, Hair, Skin, Goal and Flag - read the PROFILE answers PROFILE!$C$7, PROFILE!$C$14, PROFILE!$C$15, PROFILE!$C$17 and the 15 condition flags on PROFILE rows 36-50. One match column per sheet Every knowledge row carries a hidden match cell that resolves to 1 when the row is visible under your profile and 0 when it is not. That is the value the INTEGRITY CHECK counts and the value the dashboard's FILTER selects, so the sheets and the dashboard read the same truth. Nothing is deleted A row your profile does not match is hidden by the filter, never removed. Unhide the five tag columns and the match column on any knowledge sheet to see the full universal set and the rule that selected your subset - the helper fill on those cells stays legible when unhidden.

sections.title: THE FIRST THREE MINUTES
intro: Fill PROFILE, read the dashboard, act on one anchor habit per domain. The full programme is WEEKLY_PLAN's twelve weeks. Minute one - fill PROFILE Every yellow cell, top to bottom, including every condition flag you actually have - a flag set to Yes is what surfaces its rows. The seeded values are where the workbook starts, not advice for you. Minute two - read the dashboard MASTER_DASHBOARD is the filtered view of all six knowledge sheets under your profile. An empty section means nothing in that domain applies to you yet. Minute three - act on one anchor habit per domain WEEKLY_PLAN's daily anchors: a fixed wake time, protein at each meal, SPF every morning, a nightly retinoid, the caffeine cutoff, one zone-2 session.

sections.title: EVIDENCE GRADES
intro: A multiple RCTs or a meta-analysis · B at least one RCT or a strong prospective cohort · C small, mechanistic or observational · D theoretical or anecdotal · Rx prescription only · X not worth it How the chips use them The six knowledge sheets paint their grade chips by exactly these letters. MISTAKES grades verdicts, not papers: a refuted claim takes X and a contested one takes C even where the underlying evidence would read higher. An Rx row is prescription only - it needs a clinician.

sections.title: VISIBILITY TAGS
intro: Every knowledge row carries the five tags below in hidden columns, and it is visible only when every one of them passes. ALL always matches. A Flag list is strict on purpose: it matches only when every flag in it is set, so a partial condition never surfaces the row.

sections.title: WHERE TRAINING LIVES
intro: The WEEKLY_PLAN handoff, restated for the map: this workbook does not program workouts. GZCL owns: Exercise selection, sets, reps and load progression, warm-ups, mobility, conditioning programming - every decision that makes a session. This workbook owns: The targets that plan executes against: the body-fat band, the protein floor and ceiling, calorie guidance, the cardio dose, the recovery rules, the measurement loop. Set them on PROFILE, then execute them in GZCL Program.xlsx. The boundary test: Any sentence in this workbook that prescribes sets, reps or a session plan is a defect; its fix belongs in GZCL Program.xlsx. If that sheet runs without these targets, it is the wrong plan.

sections.title: INTEGRITY CHECK
intro: The workbook's own self-test, run live. For each knowledge sheet it reads two numbers off the hidden match column - the rows resolving to 1 under your profile, and the sheet's total data rows - scanning each sheet from its first data row down. OK means the column resolved to numbers and the 1s fit inside the rows. REVIEW means the numbers failed to resolve (a broken reference, an empty or non-numeric count) or the 1s outnumber the rows; rebuild the workbook from the data, do not edit the formulas. Nothing here judges your data - a check never fires because your profile matches nothing.

sections.title: MISTAKES
intro: A 0 is a valid answer, not a broken sheet: it says that domain holds no row your profile selects. Empty number columns on first open mean the file has not recalculated yet - recalculate once and they fill in.
